problem.paragraph: Let $$A$$ be a $$2 \times 2$$ matrix with eigenvalues $$3$$ and $$1/3$$ and corresponding eigenvectors $$\textbf{v}_{1} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 1 \\ 1 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ and $$\textbf{v}_{2} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {- 1} \\ 1 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . Let $$\{\textbf{x}_{k}\}$$ be a solution of the difference equation $$\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$$ , $$\textbf{x}_{0} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 9 \\ 1 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ .

list.item: Compute $$\textbf{x}_{1} = A\textbf{x}_{0}$$ . [Hint: You do not need to know $$A$$ itself.]
Find a formula for $$\textbf{x}_{k}$$ involving $$k$$ and the eigenvectors $$\textbf{v}_{1}$$ and $$\textbf{v}_{2}$$ .

problem.paragraph: Suppose the eigenvalues of a $$3 \times 3$$ matrix $$A$$ are $$3$$ , $$4/5$$ , and $$3/5$$ , with corresponding eigenvectors $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 1 \\ 0 \\ {- 3} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ , $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} 2 \\ 1 \\ {- 5} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ , and $$\left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {- 3} \\ {- 3} \\ 7 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . Let $$\textbf{x}_{0} = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{r} {- 2} \\ {- 5} \\ 3 \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . Find the solution of the equation $$\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$$ for the specified $$\textbf{x}_{0}$$ , and describe what happens as $$k\rightarrow \text{∞}$$ .

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 3–6, assume that any initial vector $$\textbf{x}_{0}$$ has an eigenvector decomposition such that the coefficient $$c_{1}$$ in equation (1) of this section is positive.3

problem.paragraph: Determine the evolution of the dynamical system in Example 1 when the predation parameter $$p$$ is $$\text{.2}$$ in equation (3). (Give a formula for $$\textbf{x}_{k}.)$$ Does the owl population grow or decline? What about the wood rat population?

Determine the evolution of the dynamical system in Example 1 when the predation parameter $$p$$ is $$.125$$ . (Give a formula for $$\textbf{x}_{k}$$ .) As time passes, what happens to the sizes of the owl and wood rat populations? The system tends toward what is sometimes called an unstable equilibrium. What do you think might happen to the system if some aspect of the model (such as birth rates or the predation rate) were to change slightly?

In old-growth forests of Douglas fir, the spotted owl dines mainly on flying squirrels. Suppose the predator–prey matrix for these two populations is $$A = \left\lbrack \begin{array}{rr} .4 & .3 \\ {- p} & {1.2} \end{array} \right\rbrack$$ . Show that if the predation parameter $$p$$ is $$\text{.325}$$ , both populations grow. Estimate the long-term growth rate and the eventual ratio of owls to flying squirrels.

Show that if the predation parameter $$p$$ in Exercise 5 is $$.5$$ , both the owls and the squirrels will eventually perish. Find a value of $$p$$ for which populations of both owls and squirrels tend toward constant levels. What are the relative population sizes in this case?
Let $$A$$ have the properties described in Exercise 1.

list.item: Is the origin an attractor, a repeller, or a saddle point of the dynamical system $$\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$$ ?
Find the directions of greatest attraction and/or repulsion for this dynamical system.
Make a graphical description of the system, showing the directions of greatest attraction or repulsion. Include a rough sketch of several typical trajectories (without computing specific points).

problem.paragraph: Determine the nature of the origin (attractor, repeller, or saddle point) for the dynamical system $$\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$$ if $$A$$ has the properties described in Exercise 2. Find the directions of greatest attraction or repulsion.

exercise_group.instruction: In Exercises 9–14, classify the origin as an attractor, repeller, or saddle point of the dynamical system $$\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$$ . Find the directions of greatest attraction and/or repulsion.

problem.paragraph: $$A = \left[\right. 1.7 & - .3 - 1.2 & .8 \left]\right.$$
$$A = \left[\right. .3 & .4 - .3 & 1.1 \left]\right.$$
$$A = \left[\right. .4 & .5 - .4 & 1.3 \left]\right.$$
$$A = \left[\right. .5 & .6 - .3 & 1.4 \left]\right.$$
$$A = \left[\right. .8 & .3 - .4 & 1.5 \left]\right.$$
$$A = \left[\right. 1.7 & .6 - .4 & .7 \left]\right.$$

Let $$A = \begin{bmatrix} .4 & 0 & {.2} \\ .3 & {.8} & {.3} \\ .3 & {.2} & {.5} \end{bmatrix}$$ . The vector $$\textbf{v}_{1} = \begin{bmatrix} .1 \\ .6 \\ .3 \end{bmatrix}$$ is an eigenvector for $$A$$ , and two eigenvalues are .5 and .2. Construct the solution of the dynamical system $$\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$$ that satisfies $$\textbf{x}_{0} = (0,.3,.7)$$ . What happens to $$\textbf{x}_{k}$$ as $$k\rightarrow \text{∞}$$ ?

[T] Produce the general solution of the dynamical system $$\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$$ when $$A = \begin{bmatrix} .90 & .01 & {.09} \\ .01 & {.90} & {.01} \\ .09 & {.09} & {.90} \end{bmatrix}$$ .

Construct a stage-matrix model for an animal species that has two life stages: juvenile (up to $$1$$ year old) and adult. Suppose the female adults give birth each year to an average of $$1.6$$ female juveniles. Each year, $$\text{30} \%$$ of the juveniles survive to become adults and $$80\%$$ of the adults survive. For $$k \geq 0$$ , let $$\textbf{x}_{k} = (j_{k},a_{k})$$ , where the entries in $$\textbf{x}_{k}$$ are the numbers of female juveniles and female adults in year $$k$$ .

list.item: Construct the stage-matrix $$A$$ such that $$\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$$ for $$k \geq 0$$ .
Show that the population is growing, compute the eventual growth rate of the population, and give the eventual ratio of juveniles to adults.

[T] Suppose that initially there are $$15^{}$$ juveniles and $$15$$ adults in the population. Produce four graphs that show how the population changes over eight years: (a) the number of juveniles, (b) the number of adults, (c) the total population, and (d) the ratio of juveniles to adults (each year). When does the ratio in (d) seem to stabilize? Include a listing of the program or keystrokes used to produce the graphs for (c) and (d).

problem.paragraph: A herd of American buffalo (bison) can be modeled by a stage matrix similar to that for the spotted owls. The females can be divided into calves (up to $$1$$ year old), yearlings ( $$1$$ to $$2$$ years), and adults. Suppose an average of $$42$$ female calves are born each year per $$100$$ adult females. (Only adults produce offspring.) Each year, about $$60\%$$ of the calves survive, $$75\%$$ of the yearlings survive, and $$95\%$$ of the adults survive. For $$k \geq 0$$ , let $$\textbf{x}_{k} = (c_{k},y_{k},a_{k})$$ , where the entries in $$\textbf{x}_{k}$$ are the numbers of females in each life stage at year $$k$$ .

list.item: Construct the stage-matrix $$A$$ for the buffalo herd, such that $$\textbf{x}_{k + 1} = A\textbf{x}_{k}$$ for $$k \geq 0$$ .
[T] Show that the buffalo herd is growing, determine the expected growth rate after many years, and give the expected numbers of calves and yearlings present per 100 adults.
